report:
Performed a fresh full review of crates.sage_ir.types.spans.relative_composition, not a snapshot-only refresh. Reviewed the current claim, seven implementation associations and three tests. Requirements: each source-root item has an absolute range with one ParseSource; nested placement is relative to the immediate represented owner; signature CST, body CST and typed-body nodes are relative to their own definition start; resolution composes intervening placements with the source-root range while retaining source identity. Captured the spans guide, accepted architectural rationale and actual test helpers.

Implementation chain: parse/util.rs absolute_span retains the supplied ParseSource and item start/end, while relative_span subtracts the current item base. parse/items.rs computes child placement from the owner's base, includes leading attributes in child_start, and passes that child_start to each associated function/type/constant parser. The function parser uses the new base for attributes, generics, parameters, return type, body and where clauses and gives the item CST a zero start. local_syms/associated.rs lower_item resolves placement against owner_span and gives the new symbol the resulting absolute span while retaining its independent relative CST. local_syms/mod.rs relative_span_base selects the represented item's own span, including associated functions/types/constants. diagnostic.rs resolves a relative diagnostic against that base, not the enclosing owner's base again. span.rs adds relative start/end to the base start and preserves ParseSource. infer_ctx.rs alloc_expr stores the supplied RelativeSpan unchanged in TyExpr. Together these account for the owner-placement and node-local offset composition in the represented associated-item paths. Current captured inference/diagnostic contents were inspected for these operations; unrelated recovery changes do not change their coordinate calculation.

Ordinary associated_item_origin_includes_first_attribute tests trait and impl owners, each with function/type/constant members, with and without two attributes and with a source prefix. It directly asserts owner start, one associated member, owner.start + placement.start/end against actual source offsets, child CST start zero/end equal item length, and exact relative attribute spans. These are meaningful byte-coordinate and rebase assertions across twelve combinations. parse_fixture builds a real source root and invokes production parsing; it does not supply the expected placements. This test does not inspect every signature/body/typed-node coordinate or generated source.

Ordinary moving_associated_items_preserves_symbol_query_keys covers trait/impl functions, types and constants under sibling insertion and reorder, then reverses each edit. It checks each member's owner and asserts the interned-symbol observer does not reexecute after either movement. The captured ObservedSymbol and tracked observer make this a real identity/reuse assertion. It is complementary evidence that placement does not become identity, not a direct assertion of updated absolute byte positions. It does not prove all span composition solely by a passing query-log check.

The TODO types_spans_relative_composition contains no assertions and explicitly retains the complete attributes/signatures/bodies/associated/error/zero-width/generated-text coordinate matrix before and after item/sibling movement. That deferral is justified because the ordinary tests cover associated placement/attributes and identity reuse but not all nested coordinates. Replacing it requires direct resolved-byte assertions across those source/node categories, including typed bodies, multiple represented boundaries, generated ParseSource identity, and movement. No N/A exemption or claim weakening is used; the source-root and every-intervening-range requirements remain intact.

Validation was current source inspection through fresh review start/read. No source edits or behavioral tests were performed by this reviewer; centrally passed suites remain separate execution evidence. No requested edits: current implementation and substantive partial tests are supported, while the explicit full-coordinate matrix TODO honestly retains the outstanding coverage.
